title: High Dynamic Range Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
author: Karić, Marques, et al.

steps.title: Install compensating and blocking capacitors
steps.instruction: Place a 1 pF compensating capacitor (Cc) at the preamplifier input using a tee‑piece; optionally insert a 100 pF DC‑blocking capacitor (Cb) in series to remove the DC component b₀. The 1 pF value matches the junction stray capacitance, and the 100 pF value gives low impedance for resistive harmonics across the blocker.

steps.title: Configure dual‑channel waveform generator
steps.instruction: Connect a synchronized dual‑channel waveform generator (e.g., the MLA‑3 multifrequency lock‑in) so that channel 1 outputs the excitation voltage V(t)=V_drv cos(ω₀t) and channel 2 outputs the compensation voltage V_cmp cos(ω₀t+φ) which is applied to Cc.

steps.title: Set excitation voltage and frequency
steps.instruction: Choose the excitation amplitude V_drv and frequency f=ω₀/2π as required: for imaging V_drv≈150 mV, for spectroscopy V_drv=600 mV (or 700 mV in some runs) at f=640 Hz. The maximal excitation amplitude of the generator is 12 V, which together with Cc=1 pF allows compensation currents up to ≈50 nA.

steps.title: Select preamplifier and gain
steps.instruction: Use a large‑bandwidth current preamplifier (NF corp SA‑606F2 with gain 10⁹ V/A or SA‑607F2 with gain 10¹⁰ V/A). The preamplifier bandwidth limits the highest detectable harmonic; in our setup it is 40 320 Hz, corresponding to the 63rd harmonic of the 640 Hz excitation.

steps.title: Measure system transfer function
steps.instruction: Retract the tip by a few nanometres, then for each harmonic n ω₀ apply the same AC amplitude and record the displacement current ID and its phase relative to the fundamental. From ID = C_s n ω₀ V determine the amplitude and phase transfer functions for all n to be used in compensation.

steps.title: Calculate compensation voltages
steps.instruction: For each harmonic to be removed compute the required compensation voltage amplitude so that the generated current b̃_n = Cc dV/dt equals the target resistive current. Use φ = φ_c − π/2, where φ_c≈π is the phase that cancels the stray capacitive current. Example target currents: b̃₁=3.2 nA (height‑dependence test), b̃₁=31.2 nA (spectroscopy), b̃₁=36.45 nA (topography), up to ≈50 nA (maximum achievable with 12 V drive).

steps.title: Apply active harmonic cancellation
steps.instruction: Enable channel 2 of the waveform generator to drive Cc with the calculated V_cmp. The resulting displacement current b̃_n opposes the corresponding resistive harmonic bn, compressing the total tunnelling current It_HDR = It_max − ∑|b̃_n|. Verify cancellation by monitoring the lock‑in amplitude of each harmonic; the DC component b₀ can be removed additionally by inserting Cb.

steps.title: Use Δb₁ for feedback control
steps.instruction: Monitor Δb₁ = b₁ − b̃₁ via the lock‑in. Subtract the out‑of‑contact offset so that Δb₁ → 0 at large tip‑sample distances. Use Δb₁ (or log Δb₁) as the feedback signal to maintain constant tip height; e.g., set the feedback to keep log Δb₁ = 300 pA (Δb₁ ≈ 297 pA) during topographic imaging.

steps.title: Perform spectroscopy with harmonic removal
steps.instruction: Acquire I‑V curves on the sample (e.g., Au(111)) while the chosen harmonics are actively cancelled (e.g., b̃₁=31.2 nA). Keep the DC component b₀ present unless Cb is used. Record the compressed current range (I_max reduced) and note the effective current (≈50 nA for V_drv=150 mV, gain 10⁹).

steps.title: Adjust preamplifier gain for compressed current
steps.instruction: Because harmonic removal reduces I_max, increase the preamplifier gain to the maximal value (10¹⁰ V/A) to improve signal‑to‑noise ratio. Ensure the resulting current does not exceed the gain‑limited maximum (~1 nA for gain 10¹⁰); larger currents can be compensated by increasing Cc.

steps.title: Validate LDOS preservation
steps.instruction: Numerically differentiate the acquired I‑V data to obtain dI/dV (LDOS). Verify that removal of b₀ has no effect on LDOS shape, while removal of b₁ only shifts the LDOS rigidly (e.g., surface‑state onset remains at ≈ −500 mV). Compare spectra with and without harmonic removal to confirm that spectral features are unchanged.
